# Astra v0.5.0 development trial

## Review model — Product Owner update, 2026-09-05

GitHub Codex external review was intentionally removed from the Astra lane by Product Owner decision, effective immediately during #41. Astra now owns implementation and two distinct substantive reviews: Pass A before PR creation and Pass B against the exact final PR HEAD. No further Codex requests, waiting, review-surface inspection, reviewed-SHA requirement, or review-attempt merge gate applies. Normal-lane process is unchanged. Scope, invariants, product-decision boundaries, actual field evidence, CI, frozen baseline, and experiment-only merges remain mandatory.

Normal and Astra review models differ; benchmark comparisons must account for this. Historical exception: before this update, #41 received one external finding already read and under correction. That evidence is retained below and is not relabeled as an Astra finding. The revised no-external-review model applies from this update forward; claiming the entire earlier history contained no external review would be inaccurate.

Each completed item records Pass A/Pass B findings, test-discovered defects, review-only defects, correction counts, and any later escaped defect. Final reporting uses **Astra review effectiveness** and identifies this workflow transition explicitly.

## #41 implementation and stage-1 audit

Branch: `astra/41-windows-platform`, from integration commit `0ccc6af`.
Product Owner explicitly authorized using the current #41 body despite the normal Project's Product Decision label.

Implemented bounded Host/client contracts, native SCM and local-group provisioning, virtual-account service lifetime, protected machine root, #40 runtime composition, query/start-only client activation, test-injected HKCU startup and Explorer integration, and atomic versioned CurrentUser-DPAPI client credentials with an injected generator. No production generator is supplied. SelfTest now targets Windows with authorized test-only references; the production reference graph/allowlist is unchanged.

Allowed decisions: stable service `PalworldServerManagerHost`, group `PalworldServerManagerUsers`; compact activation enum; version 1 encrypted JSON payload; caller-supplied test path/write seam; file-sharing lock serializes same-user clients; real logon helper in SelfTest; unique integration service/group/user names. The running Host never provisions itself. Existing registrations are not silently adopted. Groups and authoritative data are retained at service uninstall.

Self-review found and corrected an existing-state ACL edge in the new provisioner: securing a root alone does not remove explicit permissions from old child files/protected directories. The implementation rejects unsafe explicit child access and reparse paths before permitting the new service to start. A build found an ambiguous test-harness TimeoutException name; qualified it. These are Astra/test findings, not GitHub Codex findings.

## #41 external review round 1

PR #61 targets the experiment branch. Reviewed SHA `d2ecae8f6ed43c7448801710479ce7eaa0e7b4de`. All four review surfaces checked. Two requests were made after the initial five-minute window; GitHub Codex returned review `5122646739` and inline finding `3941740363` / thread `PRRT_kwDOT8td0c6fmFRi`.

Valid P1 finding credited to `@chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`: protected descendants containing Administrator/SYSTEM-only ACLs or a service deny ACE passed the existing-state check but prevented service startup. Correction requires protected descendants to grant the service full, non-inherit-only access; deny ACLs fail closed instead of guessing group effective access. Related self-review also rejects unprivileged child owners, who can change DACLs despite lacking an explicit data-write ACE. A dedicated regression test covers protected administrator-only state, service/group denies, outsider ownership/access, and usable protected/inheritable layouts.

Original exact-head remote evidence: CI workflow run `33985777171` PASS (169/169 plus real service/multi-user integration and successful service/group/user/profile/file cleanup); Docs run `33985778847` PASS. These establish actual virtual-account identity, DACL, boot toggles, database/lock lifecycle, non-admin rights, cross-user DPAPI, and uninstall preservation. They are pre-correction evidence; fresh runs and a fresh invariant audit are required for the correction HEAD.

Full registry re-audit of the correction: same matrix above; changes affect HOST-001/PERSIST-001/SEC-001 provisioning access and preserve the three-identity Host-state boundary. No other authority creation/executor/credential path was added. Frozen source and production dependency graph remain unchanged. No new Product Decision. External re-review was subsequently removed by Product Owner authorization; correction proceeds through Astra Pass B.

## #41 Review Pass B under revised workflow

Fresh final-diff review examined all changed files against integration `0ccc6af`, including native handle/error ownership, SCM access delegation order, runtime resource cleanup, encrypted credential concurrency, path quoting, negative tests, actual CI evidence, and privileged helper cleanup. One additional Astra-only security finding: the provisioner delegated SERVICE_START before securing the data root, allowing an existing activation-group member to race installation. Corrected by completing Host-state protection before publishing the activation DACL. Default SCM permissions do not delegate start to that group. This is a Pass B finding, independent of the earlier external protected-descendant finding.

Pass A findings: explicit permissions on existing descendants could survive root-only protection; integration group cleanup needed proof of creation. Pass B findings: protected descendants' service usability/owner/deny checks (continuation of the pre-policy external finding plus related Astra owner audit), and activation-delegation ordering. Test-discovered defect: ambiguous TimeoutException type caused the first integration-harness compile failure. Correction iterations: initial Pass A corrections, post-PR ACL regression correction, and fresh Pass B provisioning-order correction. No post-merge escaped defect known (not merged yet).

The final corrected ACL and provisioning-order suite passed locally at 170/170; Release build had zero warnings/errors and strict docs passed. Provisioning-order change requires fresh final-head remote integration. Full applicable invariant matrix re-evaluated: no changes to IDs/scope; LOCAL-003 and SEC-001 now additionally require root protection before group activation rights. Review Pass B is pending final validation and exact-head recheck; no Codex re-review will be requested or inspected.

## #27 preflight decision packet

**SHADOW PRODUCT DECISION REQUIRED** — #27 Host secure storage, parent #20. Declared dependencies now satisfied through #41. Accepted #19 section 7 describes encrypted-blob storage as readable only by the specific service account, while sections 2c/5a require privileged offline Host.Cli bootstrap/recovery to use the secure store. The exact ACL treatment of that exceptional caller is not explicit, and #27's Allowed Decisions name blob layout/key naming without authorizing a security-boundary change.

Decision requested: (A, recommended) explicitly grant the dedicated service plus elevated Administrators/SYSTEM access, matching #41's Host-root identities and #19's stated privileged-machine-owner limitation; or (B) retain a service-only DACL and separately specify the exceptional privileged access mechanism used by offline recovery. A avoids inventing impersonation/ACL-takeover behavior and still excludes ordinary users/clients; B makes direct file access narrower but requires a defined privileged recovery path. Only #27's Windows store/security integration is blocked; #43 and bounded UI design can continue without prejudging this choice. No #27 implementation has begun and no canonical issue/Project has been mutated. Product Owner input requested; unanswered is not approval.

## #42c1 preflight: per-connection LocalPrincipal authentication

A versioned, domain-separated challenge binds HostId, LocalPrincipalId, a random connection binding and a fresh random nonce. Single consumption and a 30-second monotonic deadline bound the challenge; a new challenge invalidates the prior attempt. Native OsPrincipalRef is supplied only by the already-proven platform seam.

Expected files/layers: Contracts public challenge/verification framing; BCL-only Client.Platform.Contracts production generator/signing helper (no OS dependency and no Host project path); Host.Persistence read-only active-principal lookup; Host per-connection authentication state; isolated tests and docs. Principal authentication is distinct from capabilities; the fresh-state identity hook does not implement the general permission engine. Future mutation handlers must perform their authorization check within their own transaction.

Protected-effect paths: challenge issuance, signature verification, replay/expiry, reauthentication, native SID mismatch, current persisted key/state changes, cross-connection/Host/principal substitution, malformed/noncanonical key/frame/signature input, client key generation/store/reload, and disposal/concurrent verification. Host stores/verifies only public material; ordinary clients continue using their own DPAPI credential store. ## #42c1 implementation and initial validation

Implemented the bounded [principal-authentication primitive](../developer/v0.5-local-principal-authentication.md): independent client-side P-256 key/signature handling, public Contracts frame/verifier, read-only SQLite lookup and disposable per-TLS-connection Host state. Nonces are connection/Host/principal bound, expire monotonically, and are consumed before verification. Native mismatch is rejected through an enum-only reporting hook. Current identity/key/Owner state is re-read on every authenticated use; the hook is not a grant or a cached authorization token.

Focused tests pass. Initial test-evidence correction: a private-material absence check attempted to read the live SQLite file with incompatible file sharing. It now closes the isolated writer and clears its pools before inspecting quiescent persisted Host files; client files live in a separate sibling test root. This is pre-PR correction cycle 1, not a production failure or a live-WAL backup claim. Code review also made the repository connection explicitly read-only, with a missing-root no-create test, and added strict ASCII rejection to the signer. Full local/remote validation and Review Pass A remain pending.

Pre-PR correction cycle 2: substantive review found that checking the Initialized flag alone did not reject a malformed initialized database with no active Owner, and default pooling could retain read-only database handles beyond the Host writer's shutdown cleanup. Added the Owner-cardinality predicate to the same query snapshot and disabled pooling for these owned lookups. New tests reject an active row on an uninitialized Host and an ownerless initialized Host, and verify exclusive file access after closing only the Host writer pool. The prior uninitialized fixture had no row at all, so its rejection did not prove the initialization predicate; that evidence gap is now closed. Added a synthetic committed Owner-state transition to prove the identity hook reads current Owner status and revocation, plus a DPAPI-reloaded production client key authenticating against its actual persisted public verifier. These are primitive tests, not recovery/enrollment ceremony or multi-user field passes.

## #42d1 discovery: escaped #42c2 grant-helper defect

While composing Owner re-home, reviewing architecture section 5's exact forest rule exposed a latent defect in PR #74's shared InvalidateGrants helper: its seed included GrantedByLocalPrincipalId as well as GranteeLocalPrincipalId. Ordinary non-Owner delegated grants normally descend from that actor's held grant, so the existing non-Owner tests did not distinguish the redundant issuer seed. For the displaced Owner, however, it would invalidate every independently issued root grant to other actors, violating the explicit per-subtree rule (not every grant an actor ever issued). This escaped both #42c2 reviews and was discovered before #42d1 integration. Fix the helper to seed only grants HELD by the revoked principal, then traverse DerivedFromGrantId descendants; add recovery regression evidence for independent Owner-issued roots and descendant cascades in both grant tables. Update the implementation document's corresponding claim. This is #42d1 correction cycle 1, and an escaped prior-unit defect, not a product-decision ambiguity. Historical #42c2 clean/no-known-defect statements remain snapshots, superseded by this finding; the audit must be repeated after validation.

Compose the accepted authentication and enrollment primitives into bounded protobuf/gRPC methods over the accepted Windows TLS named pipe. Protected paths: one disposable protocol/authentication session per actual HTTP/2 TLS connection; native SID supplied only by the Windows platform connection feature, never request input; explicit protocol-major/capability negotiation before security methods; principal challenges/proofs and per-request fresh identity lookup; no capability grants inferred from identity/Owner flag. Raw enrollment/handoff material is confined to authenticated request/response buffers and never logged. Owner invitation output is explicit to its authorized caller; Host persists only the existing keyed verifier. ## #42d3c2 preflight: ordinary-client security composition

Base dda3a4ffddfd9f085c91be82c76d954d1928691e; branch astra/42-client-security-composition. Implement one shared source coordinator compiled into ordinary CLI and Avalonia, with a Windows composition using their existing client-only platform seams. No new product project-reference edges and no Host/Core/persistence/Host-platform dependency in either client. Standard Grpc.Net.Client plus protobuf messages and a private typed CallInvoker adapter avoid duplicate generated service types in the self-test assembly. Tests compile the same shared source and use the actual production listener builder.

Protected paths: read the protected public trust anchor; exact TLS/HTTP2/HostId/protocol/feature negotiation before any credential transmission; activate/query-start only after a precisely classified LocalHostEndpointUnavailableException, never based on a generic gRPC status or a TLS failure; new channel/session per command, without retrying mutations automatically. Load only the current user's DPAPI key, sign the bounded Host/principal challenge, clear caller-owned private buffers, and distinguish authenticated identity/Owner status from capability grants. Owner invitation/removal remain RPCs with Host-side authorization. Invitation secret output is explicit authorized delivery, not diagnostics; completion reads the enrollment code from standard input rather than process arguments.

For protected bootstrap/rotation/re-home artifacts and enrollment codes: preserve the exact Host/ticket/purpose/key-choice context in the durable ceremony store before sending a public key; authenticate the returned principal using that prepared key before ConfirmAsync; require actual Owner status for Owner ceremonies; delete a protected artifact only after durable confirmation. A lost response/cancellation never discards pending keys. Existing active re-home targets reuse their key only after it authenticates; a failed proof is not treated as credential absence. No client offline preparation, machine recovery, Owner setter, direct database write, remote transport or arbitrary endpoint/path switch. Runtime-owned protobuf/string copies are never logged; only owned buffers can be cleared.

CLI supplies bounded identity, invitation/removal, enrollment completion and protected-handoff completion commands. Avalonia receives the same coordinator through its composition root for later authorized screens; this unit adds no feature screen or operational UI. Final real two-user/Owner ceremonies with the shipped clients remain c3. Audit all registry families, especially CLIENT-001-003, LOCAL-001-004, OWNER-001/002, SEC-001, PROTO-001, HOST-002, PERSIST-001 and PLATFORM-001/002. Acceptance tests cover actual pinned RPC authentication/completion, lost-result/retry with the same durable key, confirmation-before-deletion, wrong pin and unknown principal without activation/authority, malformed/incompatible negotiation, Owner-only invitation/removal, rotation/re-home key selection and safe errors. Full build/suite/docs, applicable actual Windows CI, stale-reference/invariant audit and two reviews required; do not waive the final c3 field contract.

Initial coordinator/CLI/lazy Avalonia composition builds with zero warnings and no new product graph edge. Review cycle A1 identified a re-home lost-result gap before tests: a revoked target can retain an old bound client credential, then be reactivated under the same principal ID with a fresh pending key. Recomputing key choice on retry would challenge that now-active ID and fail proof with the old current key before reaching the pending key. Extend the client-only ceremony store with a read-only exact-ticket context lookup (pending or most recent completed, with retired/mismatched context refusal), and reuse its recorded key choice before attempting any new selection. This is public metadata only, with the same DPAPI/file-lock validation; no new persistence writer, authority or schema version. Add a real Host transaction/lost-reply regression for that revoked-target path. No pending state is discarded to recover from transport failure.

## #44a guarded SPAKE2 wrapper preflight

Product Owner approved all three recommended guards and continuous development. Base `fd5322a528489beab0f80ae4071292e0f6185c9c`; branch `astra/44-guarded-spake2`. Bounded unit: pinned Pakery P-256 native wrapper, Windows managed platform seam, authenticated post-confirmation identity binding, native build/qualification tests and docs. No remote listener, durable PeerBound/Active transition, capability grants, rotation or revocation in this unit; those follow after accepted primitive integration. Authority/credential paths: pairing code enters only Host-side platform API, ephemeral key remains native, only confirmed identity-binding operations are exposed; existing Host private credentials are not read by this wrapper. No persistence writer, operation executor or ordinary-client dependency changes.

Native sessions use non-reused integer handles and serialized access; every failed operation discards the session, disposal is idempotent, no cleared output is ever verified and no raw key export exists. Managed lifetime guards duplicate those guarantees, support cancellation and redact failures. Confirmations are exactly 32 bytes, key shares uncompressed P-256 exactly 65 bytes. Versioned context binds the session nonce; deterministic test features are excluded from the shipped wrapper. Code derivation/profile, randomness failure, malformed/late calls, altered HostId/credential and native loading need actual managed-boundary evidence. Re-audit all forty invariants and exact A/B heads. Test qualification is not full #44 completion or independent audit. No outside input is required.

## #46d Host-owned worker lifetime — preflight

Base3fd53bf88e128f81ae3130d8116d8ecbf8398fa2 after PR151. Current46 body unchanged, complete Project39/39 refreshed; prerequisites33/19/40/43/45 and internal46a/b/c satisfied. This keeps review bounded without dropping an acceptance criterion or inventing concrete destructive recovery semantics. Acceptance checkpoint Docs34177326912 is running and remains an acceptance-record check, not new executable qualification.

Scope: an internal trusted Host operation runtime with code-registered definitions/executors, atomic repository admission, operation-scoped execution contexts and tracked worker tasks. Client admission cancellation ends at commit; accepted workers receive only the runtime's own shutdown token, with no ambient request ExecutionContext flow. Context mutations require explicit trusted current-authority callbacks and keep repository revision/lock guarantees. A stopped/failed/unfinished worker cannot automatically resolve its record or release exclusion. Shutdown refuses new work and drains actual workers before disposal returns; the enclosing Host must retain its machine lease until then. No network-generation or client-connection lifetime owns the worker runtime.

Read-only observations distinguish actual tracked workers, terminal records and unresolved startup records. Every existing nonterminal Host/server record is inspected; manual/unknown/inconsistent work is RecoveryRequired and known other dispositions are AwaitingRecovery, never reported as Running. This unit does not apply startup recovery handlers; the next bounded unit must explicitly apply per-phase retry/resume/discard before whole46 acceptance. No concrete server operation, raw client executor/SQL input, business audit invention, offline queue or retry-all behavior.

Expected changes: new internal Host worker/context types; representative self-tests/registration; worker documentation and ledger. No schema, grant writer, credentials, dependencies, client/Contracts/wire, platform, production composition, frozen WPF/Lan or Linux change. Existing WindowsHostComposition owns the actual production lease; this framework is not yet installed into its RPC/composition path. All normal authoritative mutation remains through accepted OperationRepository under caller-held machine exclusion.

Applicable HOST-001/002, PERSIST-001, IDENT-002, LOCAL-001, AUTH-003, OPS-001/002/003/004, RECOVERY-001, SEC-001 plus complete40 audit.
